html:
The Yinhawangka, also spelt Inawongga, are an Aboriginal Australian people of the inland Pilbara in Western Australia, in the hills of the upper Ashburton River. The map shows them from 1600 to 1815.

Their neighbours included the Banyjima to the north, the Jurruru and Jiwarli to the west and the Ngalawangka to the east. Little was written about them before the 20th century. Like much of the Pilbara, their country later became sheep and cattle stations and then, from the 1960s, iron ore mining land.
